title: fix: use Mistral direct for Large 3 fallback
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Keeps `mistralai/mistral-large-3` on Azure (`myceli-prod-eastus`, deployment `Mistral-Large-3`); aliases `mistral-large-3`/`mistral-large`, multiplier 0.75, Quest access, and no Pollinations GPU remain unchanged.
- Replaces the reproducibly failing OpenRouter/Mistral-ZDR fallback (404: no endpoints) with Mistral direct `api.mistral.ai/v1`, checkpoint `mistral-large-2512`. Removes the OpenRouter fee from fallback costs; public pricing stays unchanged. Maps `seed` to `random_seed` to avoid upstream 422s.
- Leaves Small 4 direct and Small 3.2 on its existing routes: neither exact checkpoint appears in our Azure account catalog, and Mistral direct no longer lists Small 3.2. [Provider model/pricing](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-3-25-12).
- Validation: 110 Gen routing/billing/resolver tests, 468 catalog-consumer tests, Gen typecheck, Biome, and diff checks pass. Live Azure Chat/Responses and direct Mistral text, terminal streaming usage, tools, seeded JSON/sampling probes pass.
- Draft verification gaps: no existing local test credential in expected locations, so forced-fallback E2E, wallet/Tinybird reconciliation, cache and load checks remain pending. Vision returned HTTP 200 but misidentified a red test image; vision correctness and direct-account privacy equivalence to the previous ZDR route remain unverified. No secrets or deployments changed.

gist.headline: Large 3 Finds Its Way Home
gist.blurb: Mistral Large 3’s fallback route has stopped wandering into a provider with no endpoint. When Azure needs a hand, the hive now calls Mistral directly—and seeded requests arrive with the right name tag.
gist.summary: Replaced the failing OpenRouter/Mistral-ZDR fallback for Mistral Large 3 with Mistral’s direct api.mistral.ai/v1 endpoint using the mistral-large-2512 checkpoint, while translating seed to random_seed for upstream compatibility.
gist.impact: Mistral Large 3 aliases retain their existing Azure primary route, pricing, Quest access, and 0.75 multiplier, while fallback requests now have a working direct route and seeded generation avoids 422 errors.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy routing garden shows the Mistral Large 3 request leaving an Azure cloud terminal and following a clearly marked backup path to a friendly direct Mistral telescope-like API station. Polli, wearing a tiny route-planner cap, adjusts a seed packet labeled random_seed beside glowing code-plants, making the provider handoff feel reliable and deliberate.
